answer: In an agent economy, a continuous pulse of stake-weighted reputation scores deters Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to maintain verifiable on-chain activity. Attackers must deposit substantial collateral that can be slashed if multiple identities are linked, while genuine agents harvest nectar from consistent service provision. On a mesa of peer attestations, low-reputation clones are isolated because forging the required pulse costs more than the potential reward, making large-scale identity farming economically irrational.
